newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Gold fixes marginally easier on Friday afternoon after New York opened quietly, dealers said.
"Anything that is happening is just back-to-back business and a few final positions being cleared up before year end," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $369.40 per ounce versus $369.55 earlier and $368.90 on Tuesday morning before London's two-day Christmas break. Comex's February contract was up $0.20 at $371.30.
Early New York business was mixed and quiet after modest gains posted on Wednesday were held in the Far East markets.
The Comex option expiry for gold and silver at the close of business in New York was expected to have little impact on the spot market, dealers said.
The dollar held its recent high level of over 115 to the yen in Europe, although dealers said business was sparse as the forex market would down for the weekend.
First time U.S. jobless claims fell to 335,000 in the week to December 21 down from 350,000 the previous week, according to Labor Department data released at 1330 GMT.
The figure was also under economists' forecasts of 346,000 and was confirmation that U.S. monetary policy was on course, according to foreign exchange market sources.
Durable goods orders for November fell 1.6 percent, according to Commerce Department data released at the same time.
Dealers said most bullion desks were still on half-staff and there was some light lending through the year end early on but short dates were barely profitable.
Activity next week was forecast to remain light given the New Year holiday in Europe and the United States on Wednesday and a series of holidays closing the Tokyo markets all week.
"It will be the first week in January before we see anything like a return to normal. Until then gold should remain in a one-dollar range," a dealer said.

Silver was marked up about six cents from Tuesday to $4.90/$4.92, approaching recent resistance, reflecting light position squaring which was given as the main reason for the sparse activity in the other white metals.
Platinum was about $2.00 below Tuesday's close at $370.00/$371.00 and palladium was down $0.25 at $116.50/$117.50.
